title: Principal localization of a relative global complete intersection, with the presentation adding one variable
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Let $h\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, let $g\in T$ be its image, and let $T_g$ be the localization of $T$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Regard $f_1,\dots,f_c,h$ as elements of $R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]$. Then $T'=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$ (with $n+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations) is a relative global complete intersection, and the $R$-algebra homomorphism $T'\to T_g$ with $x_i\mapsto(x_i\bmod(f))/1$ for $i\le n$ and $x_{n+1}\mapsto1/g$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection, line 36640), part (2), proof line 36665 ('S_g = S[x_{n+1}]/(g x_{n+1} - 1)'), with the base change part (1) and Lemma 00P4 for the fibres; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00SS,algebra-lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection)
